title: The camera sees the curb
topic: Dallas puts AI cameras on 50 bulky trash trucks to photograph curbs for possible code problems, and the film follows one photo through blurring, scoring, an analyst's desk and a door to show where a person still decides.
hook: Why is this trash truck taking pictures?

treatment.logline: An eager camera on a Dallas bulky trash truck wants to photograph every curb, and the film follows one of its snapshots until it becomes a polite note or a knock on the door, with a person at every step that slows it down.
treatment.cold_open: A blue bulky trash truck rolls past a brick ranch on a Dallas street. The camera on its side, which has a face, blinks awake and snaps the tall grass. Before second three the still pops out like an instant photo.
treatment.turn: The heat map pours south, 13,800 of 20,000 photos. The director lays his route map and the residents' own complaint map over it and they match, yet the notice rates still differ, so the question stays open on screen.
treatment.button: Weeks later the same truck passes the same yard with the grass cut. The camera snaps a tidy curb and winks, and back at her desk the analyst stamps the new photo NOTHING. A person decides what happens next.

hero.name: the curb camera with a face
hero.why: a round white camera bolted to the truck's side whose lens is one big eye with brows. It wakes, snaps, squints when it blurs a face and droops when it cannot read a plate, so every step of the mechanism has a face to read. No earlier film has drawn it.

throughline.object: one instant photo of a brick ranch with tall grass

states.state: pops fresh out of the camera, tall grass, a waving neighbour, a car at the curb
the neighbour's face and the car plate fog over to soft blur
a yellow blight score tag reading 2 clips onto its corner
stamped COURTESY NOTICE and slipped into the mailbox, no case opened
a new photo of the same yard, grass cut, stamped NOTHING by the analyst

scenes.vo: Since mid-April, fifty bulky trash trucks in Dallas have carried a camera. On their routes, it snaps still photos of the curb.

draw.subject: the side camera on the trash truck
draw.action: blinks awake and snaps the tall grass of a brick ranch as the truck rolls

draw.subject: an instant photo
draw.action: pops out of the camera and flips into view, tall grass in it

draw.subject: the truck
draw.action: rolls on down the street, the camera flashing at each house it passes
draw.emotion: a neighbour on the lawn waves at it

draw.subject: the camera
draw.action: fires a flash that rings outward at the curb

scenes.vo: Not video. Stills. Each goes to software from a company called City Detect, which looks for trouble.

draw.subject: a film strip
draw.action: tears away and leaves single photos fluttering

draw.subject: the photo
draw.action: rises into a cloud where a scanning box sweeps across it

scenes.vo: Tall grass. Weeds. Litter. A car on the lawn. Peeling paint. One house got flagged for its chimney paint.

draw.subject: a yellow box
draw.action: snaps around the tall grass in a photo

draw.subject: a yellow box
draw.action: snaps around a car parked on a lawn in the next photo

draw.subject: a yellow box
draw.action: snaps around flaking paint on a wall

draw.subject: a chimney on a roof
draw.action: gets a box and a score tag slapped on it while a puff of smoke coughs out
draw.emotion: the chimney's owner on the lawn looks up, baffled

scenes.vo: The software blurs faces and license plates. One photo the city released had a black box reading motor vehicle.

draw.subject: the instant photo, filling the frame
draw.action: fogs the waving neighbour into a soft blur
draw.emotion: the camera in the corner squints, a little embarrassed

draw.subject: the car's plate
draw.action: smears into a pale bar

draw.subject: a second photo
draw.action: slides in and a black box reading motor vehicle slams over its plate
draw.emotion: the camera's eye droops, it cannot read it either

scenes.vo: The blur slips, though. The company says it works about ninety nine percent of the time. When reporters found a plate it missed, the city asked for every photo to go through the blur again.

draw.subject: the camera on the truck
draw.action: winces as a parked car's plate stays sharp in its viewfinder

draw.subject: one sharp plate in a wall of photos
draw.action: pulses inside a red ring

draw.subject: the wall of photos
draw.action: re-blurs in a wave from left to right

scenes.vo: In four months, the cameras photographed more than twenty thousand concerns.

draw.subject: a storm of photos
draw.action: pours over the analyst's desk and piles into a leaning tower
draw.emotion: the analyst throws her hands up, wide-eyed

scenes.vo: Too many to read. So each flagged property gets a blight score from one to four, and the photos are ranked so staff know which to look at first.

draw.subject: a yellow score tag reading 2
draw.action: clips onto the corner of the photo with a bounce

draw.subject: a stack of photos
draw.action: shuffles itself so the highest scores rise to the top of the analyst's queue

scenes.vo: A flag is not a ticket. A person reviews it. Staff can do nothing, keep watching, send a courtesy notice, ask for an inspection or call a city crew.

draw.subject: the analyst
draw.action: pulls the grass photo off the top of the stack and studies it

draw.subject: five round stamps
draw.action: light up one by one under her hand, nothing, watch, notice, inspect, crew

draw.subject: the WATCH stamp
draw.action: rises and glows under her hand

draw.subject: the notice stamp
draw.action: thumps down on the photo

scenes.vo: A courtesy notice opens no case and sets no deadline. A citation comes only after an officer inspects in person, gives notice, and the problem is still there.

draw.subject: the stamped photo
draw.action: slides into the mailbox while a case folder beside it stays shut and a calendar stays blank

draw.subject: the resident
draw.action: opens the mailbox door and peers in

draw.subject: a code officer
draw.action: walks up to a different house down the street and knocks
draw.emotion: that neighbour opens the door, wary

draw.subject: the officer
draw.action: points at the tall grass and checks a box on a tablet

scenes.vo: The city's own maps raise a question. Of the 20,000, about 13,800 came from southern Dallas. Could older blocks with less money for repairs get more scrutiny?

draw.subject: a map of Dallas
draw.action: fills with tiny camera flashes

draw.subject: a dashed line
draw.action: draws across the city map splitting north from south

draw.subject: the photos on the map
draw.action: slide into two stacks, a tall one of 13,800 in the south and a short one of 7,300 for the rest of the city

draw.subject: an older resident on a porch in southern Dallas
draw.action: lowers a notice and frowns at the passing truck

scenes.vo: Code compliance director Chris Christian says the trucks cover the whole city, and the camera map matches what residents report almost exactly.

draw.subject: the director
draw.action: traces blue route lines across every part of the city map on his board

draw.subject: blue route lines
draw.action: draw themselves across the whole map

draw.subject: a map of residents' own complaints
draw.action: lays over the camera map and the two line up

scenes.vo: Still, under two percent of southern flags became notices, against more than four percent in the rest of the city. The question stays open.

draw.subject: two glass jars of photos
draw.action: fill, and only a sliver of each turns into notices, the rest of the city's sliver twice as thick

draw.subject: the rest of the city's jar
draw.action: lights its green sliver and the sliver doubles the south one

draw.subject: a question mark
draw.action: drops between the jars and wobbles
draw.emotion: the analyst tilts her head, unsure

scenes.vo: Now the notices are changing. They will carry a QR code to a city help page, and council members asked for Spanish versions.

draw.subject: the notice the resident pulls from the mailbox
draw.action: draws a QR code in square by square
draw.emotion: the resident raises a phone to scan it

draw.subject: the phone screen
draw.action: opens a help page with a house and a wrench icon

draw.subject: a second notice in Spanish
draw.action: slides out from behind the first

scenes.vo: The city says about eight in ten owners fix it after a notice. The camera sees the curb. A person decides what happens next.

draw.subject: the resident
draw.action: pushes a mower through the tall grass, leaving a cut stripe

draw.subject: the truck
draw.action: rolls past again and the camera snaps the tidy yard, no box appears

draw.subject: the analyst's hand
draw.action: presses the NOTHING stamp onto the new photo of the tidy yard
